text.p: Middlesbrough, who drew 1-1 at Leeds, and Sunderland, 1-0 losers at Wimbledon, were both relegated from the English premier league on Sunday.
They will join already-doomed Nottingham Forest in the first division next season.
Coventry, 2-1 winners at Tottenham, and Southampton, despite losing 1-0 at Aston Villa, staged dramatic escapes on the final afternoon of the season.

While two of the North East's clubs were plunged into despair, there was delight at Newcastle, who thumped Forest 5-0 at St James' Park to finish as runners-up behind champions Manchester United to take the second spot in the expanded European Cup.
Arsenal, 3-1 winners at Derby, finished third while Liverpool, who drew 1-1 at Sheffield Wednesday, were fourth.
Manchester United were presented with the league trophy for the fourth time in five seasons before their home match against West Ham which they won 2-0.
